messages.author: ec0fcb6138faa0e7
messages.subject: Error in appendSpeciesNames
parts:
I keep getting an error. I am running the appendSpeciesNames in the camtrapR package. This systematically goes through all of the photo's I have in a directory and adds my species name into the file name from the metadata.
The code I use is this.

     checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = "SECRimagesOUT",            
                                             IDfrom = "metadata",                      
                                             hasCameraFolders = FALSE,        
                                             metadataSpeciesTag = "Species"
                                             metadataHeirarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                             removeNames = FALSE,
                                             writecsv = FALSE)


 It works fine until I get to the 7th folder and then I get this warning:

     Warning: out 07: metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'Hierarchicalsubject'.


Followed by this error.

     Error in rep(dirs_short[i], times =nrow(metadata.tmp)) : invalid 'times' argument


I'm pretty sure this error is referring to line 146 of the code in this link:

https://github.com/cran/camtrapR/blob/master/R/appendSpeciesNames.R


But here is a copy paste of the line of code I think the error is referring to:

      metadata.tmp <- cbind(station = rep(dirs_short[i], times = nrow(metadata.tmp)), metadata.tmp)


The exact same code for another directory (inDir = "SECRimagesIN") works perfectly.

When I tried a different function for the same image directory I have the error with, I get caught out at the exact same folder before a different error occurs.

        checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = "SECRimagesOUT",            
                                             IDfrom = "metadata",                      
                                             hasCameraFolders = FALSE,        
                                             metadataSpeciesTag = "Species"
                                             metadataHeirarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                             maxDeltaTime = 5,
                                             writecsv = FALSE)
The error in this instance is

      error: $operator is invalid for atomic vectors.

But it comes with the same warning message.

The only thing that is different about his folder is that there are no images with the "Species' tag that I specify with the metadataSpeciesTag argument. When I add a species tag to even just one image it seems to work only to be caught up at the next folder that lacks an image with the "Species" tag.

Does anyone have any suggestions. Is the function only able to deal with a directory that has the tag in each of the folders? If so is there an alternative?

Cheers

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Error in appendSpeciesNames
parts:
Hi Shannon,
well spotted. Thank you. You answered you question already. This is a bug that occurs when trying to extract metadata species IDs and no image in a station directory has a species tag, So far only the function recordTable handled this situation (see this related post), but from the next release on all functions that extract species IDs from metadata will handle this situation by giving a warning and skipping the station. 
A quick fix would be to assign a species tag to at least one image per directory. But this is of course nothing but a emergency solution. 

Please see the attached files. They contain the two functions in question (appendSpeciesNames and checkSpeciesIdentification) plus another file containing some helper funcitons. Run them all and then try again with your directories without species tags. 

One more minor thing, probably just a copy&paste mistake. In your first function call above, you probably mean appendSpeciesNames, not checkSpeciesIdentification. Besides, there is a typo in your function call (see below) and arguments metadataHierarchyDelimitor, removeNames and writecsv don't need to be included in the function call because you use the defaut of those arguments.

     appendSpeciesNames(inDir = "SECRimagesOUT",

IDfrom = "metadata",                      
                        hasCameraFolders = FALSE,        
                        metadataSpeciesTag = "Species"

removeNames = FALSE,
                        writecsv = FALSE)
